title: AHISF prototype experiment: REST/JSON vs gRPC/Protobuf

environment.topology: Client and server run as distinct operating-system processes on the same Linux host, communicating over IPv4 loopback (127.0.0.1).
environment.security: Plaintext HTTP/1.1 and gRPC over HTTP/2; TLS/mTLS disabled.

method.arrival_model: open-loop scheduled arrivals; medium workload uses periodic burst remapping
method.rest_server: Uvicorn/Starlette in separate server process; keep-alive enabled
method.connection_reuse: HTTP connection pooling via requests.Session; one reusable gRPC channel per client worker thread
method.validation: Every completed response checked for request id, payload length and SHA-256
method.tail_latency_aggregation: Request-level latency samples pooled across 10 independent validation trials; median trial p99 and bootstrap 95% CI also reported
method.latency_definition: p50/p95/p99 are scheduled-arrival-to-response completion latency; service_p99 excludes client-side executor queue time
method.resource_note: CPU sums benchmark-client and server-process CPU time, divided by elapsed time and CPU affinity count. RSS is the sum of separately sampled client/server peak RSS. Network bytes are encoded application request+response bytes, not packet-captured wire bytes.

workloads.name: medium_bursty
workloads.description: 4-KiB request, 420 offered requests/s, periodic burst arrivals

interpretation_limitations: This prototype evaluates only semantically compatible synchronous request-response adapters.
REST uses HTTP/1.1 JSON with Base64 payloads; gRPC uses HTTP/2 and dynamically described Protocol Buffer messages.
No broker or shared-memory adapter is substituted for request-response because those mechanisms have different contracts or topology constraints.
This is a separate-process, single-host loopback microbenchmark, not a cross-host, Kubernetes, Mininet, production-trace, TLS, or service-mesh evaluation.
AHISF selection is based on per-workload measured candidate profiles. Runtime orchestration and live production canary rollout are not implemented.
AHISF decision windows are built from disjoint calibration trial blocks; they are independent controller observations, while the validation set remains held out.
